questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: What is living; biodiversity; need for classification
questions.question: Which of the following is regarded as the defining feature of life?

solution.key_concept: The defining properties of life are metabolism, consciousness and cellular organisation. Cellular organisation is the defining feature of life.
steps: Growth occurs in non-living crystals and mountains as well, so it does not define life.
Reproduction is absent in sterile mules and worker bees, so it does not define life either.
Cellular organisation is the defining feature of life.
solution.why_not_others: Growth and increase in mass are also seen in non-living objects that grow by external accumulation. Reproduction is absent in some living organisms.
solution.common_trap: Treating growth or reproduction as defining properties of life.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: What is living; biodiversity; need for classification
questions.question: In which of the following are growth and reproduction synonymous?
options: Unicellular organisms that grow by cell division
Sterile hybrids such as the mule

solution.key_concept: Unicellular organisms grow by cell division, so in them growth and reproduction are the same process.
steps: In a unicellular organism, cell division increases the number of individuals.
This same cell division is also how the organism grows.
Therefore growth and reproduction are synonymous in unicellular organisms.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Unicellular organisms that grow by cell division
solution.why_not_others: Mules and worker bees do not reproduce. Crystals are non-living and grow only by surface accumulation.
solution.common_trap: Equating the growth of crystals with growth in living beings, which is intrinsic.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: What is living; biodiversity; need for classification
questions.question: Approximately how many species of organisms have been described so far?

solution.key_concept: Biodiversity is the number and types of organisms on Earth. About 1.7 to 1.8 million species have been described.
steps: Recall the number of described species: about 1.7 to 1.8 million.
Check that the unit is million, not thousand.
solution.why_not_others: Each of the other options has the correct digits but the wrong order of magnitude.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up thousand and million, or shifting the decimal point.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: What is living; biodiversity; need for classification
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Reproduction cannot be taken as a defining property of living organisms.
statements.R: All living organisms, including mules and worker bees, are capable of reproduction.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Reproduction is not a defining property of life because some living organisms do not reproduce.
steps: A sterile mule and a worker bee are living but do not reproduce.
So A is true.
R wrongly claims that these organisms can reproduce, so R is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A is true but R is false
solution.why_not_others: R is false, so any option that treats R as true is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Assuming every living organism must be able to reproduce.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: What is living; biodiversity; need for classification
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Metabolic reactions demonstrated in vitro in a test tube are not living things, but they are living reactions.
statements.II: Growth by accumulation of material on the outer surface, as seen in mountains, is characteristic of living organisms.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: In vitro metabolic reactions are living reactions but not living things. Growth in living beings is from inside, while non-living objects grow by surface accumulation.
steps: Statement I matches the notes, so it is correct.
Surface accumulation is the way non-living objects such as mountains grow.
Growth in living organisms is intrinsic, so Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement II reverses the difference between living and non-living growth, so options 1 and 4 fail. Statement I is true, so option 2 fails.
solution.common_trap: Treating any increase in size as living growth.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Taxonomy and systematics
questions.question: Giving a correct scientific name to an organism is termed

solution.key_concept: Taxonomy has four basic processes: characterisation, identification, nomenclature and classification.
steps: Nomenclature means giving an organism a correct scientific name.
Identification places the organism correctly, and classification arranges it into groups.
solution.why_not_others: Identification means correct placement. Classification means grouping. Characterisation means describing structure, development and ecology.
solution.common_trap: Confusing identification with nomenclature.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Taxonomy and systematics
questions.question: Systematics is broader than taxonomy because it additionally includes

solution.key_concept: Systematics equals taxonomy plus evolutionary relationships.
steps: Taxonomy already covers characterisation, identification, nomenclature and classification.
Systematics adds evolutionary relationships between organisms.
solution.why_not_others: Nomenclature, identification and morphological description are already part of taxonomy.
solution.common_trap: Thinking that taxonomy and systematics are exactly the same.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Taxonomy and systematics
questions.question: Which pair correctly gives the origin of the word systematics and the title of the work by Linnaeus that reflects it?

solution.key_concept: Systematics comes from the Latin word systema, meaning systematic arrangement. Linnaeus used the title Systema Naturae.
steps: The root word is systema, and it is Latin.
The work by Linnaeus is titled Systema Naturae.
Only option 4 has both parts correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Latin word systema; Systema Naturae
solution.why_not_others: Each of the other options has the wrong language, the wrong root word, the wrong title, or a combination of these.
solution.common_trap: Assuming the root word is Greek.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Taxonomy and systematics
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Describing structure, cell structure, development and ecological information

solution.key_concept: Each of the four basic processes of taxonomy has a specific meaning.
steps: Characterisation is describing structure, development and ecology (III).
Identification is placing an organism correctly (IV).
Nomenclature is giving a correct scientific name (II).
Classification is arranging organisms into groups (I).
solution.why_not_others: The other options swap identification with nomenclature, or characterisation with another process.
solution.common_trap: Swapping identification and nomenclature.
solution.time_saving_tip: Fix C-II first, since naming is unambiguous, then eliminate options.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Taxonomy and systematics
questions.question: Which of the following statements about taxonomy and systematics are correct?

statements.A: Early taxonomy was based mainly on morphology.
statements.B: Modern taxonomy also uses biochemical and molecular data besides anatomy and embryology.
statements.C: Systematics is narrower in scope than taxonomy.
statements.D: Taxonomic studies of plants, animals and microbes are useful in agriculture, forestry and industry.
statements.E: Characterisation excludes ecological information about an organism.

options: A, B, D and E only

solution.key_concept: Taxonomy has moved from morphology to multiple sources of data. Systematics is broader than taxonomy.
steps: A is true: early taxonomy used morphology.
B is true: modern taxonomy uses cytology, anatomy, embryology, physiology, biochemistry and molecular data.
C is false: systematics is broader than taxonomy because it adds evolutionary relationships.
D is true.
E is false: characterisation includes ecological information.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A, B and D only
solution.why_not_others: Options 1 and 2 include C, which is false. Options 2 and 3 include E, which is false.
solution.common_trap: Thinking systematics is a subset of taxonomy.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Concept of species and taxonomical hierarchy
questions.question: In plant classification, which rank is used in place of phylum?

solution.key_concept: Phylum is the rank used for animals. Division is the equivalent rank used for plants.
steps: The rank above Class and below Kingdom is called Phylum in animals.
In plants, this rank is called Division.
solution.why_not_others: Order, Class and Family are separate ranks used for both plants and animals.
solution.common_trap: Thinking Class replaces Phylum in plants.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Concept of species and taxonomical hierarchy
questions.question: On moving from species to kingdom in the taxonomic hierarchy,
options: Common characters increase and the number of organisms decreases
Both common characters and the number of organisms increase
Both common characters and the number of organisms decrease
Common characters decrease and the number of organisms increases

solution.key_concept: Higher ranks include more organisms but share fewer common characters.
steps: A kingdom contains far more organisms than a species.
Because it contains so many different organisms, those organisms share fewer characters.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Common characters decrease and the number of organisms increases
solution.why_not_others: Options 1, 2 and 3 get the direction of at least one of the two trends wrong.
solution.common_trap: Assuming that bigger groups share more characters.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Concept of species and taxonomical hierarchy
questions.question: In the classification of mango, Sapindales and Anacardiaceae respectively represent

solution.key_concept: Mango is classified as Plantae, Angiospermae, Dicotyledonae, Sapindales, Anacardiaceae, Mangifera, indica.
steps: Sapindales is the Order.
Anacardiaceae is the Family; the suffix -aceae indicates a family.
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 reverses the two ranks. Class is Dicotyledonae and Division is Angiospermae, so options 2 and 3 are wrong.
solution.common_trap: Reversing order and family.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Concept of species and taxonomical hierarchy
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Felidae and Canidae are placed together in the order Carnivora.
statements.R: An order is a group of related genera.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: A genus is a group of related species, a family is a group of related genera, and an order is a group of related families.
steps: Carnivora includes the families Felidae and Canidae, so A is true.
An order groups related families, not related genera, so R is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A is true but R is false
solution.why_not_others: R is false, so options 1, 2 and 4 are ruled out.
solution.common_trap: Confusing which rank groups which lower rank.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Concept of species and taxonomical hierarchy
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: In the classification of the housefly, Insecta is the class, Diptera is the order and Muscidae is the family.
statements.II: Higher taxonomic categories are more difficult to define because they are aggregates of characters.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: The housefly is classified as Arthropoda, Insecta, Diptera, Muscidae, Musca domestica. Higher ranks are aggregates of characters.
steps: The ranks given for the housefly match the notes, so Statement I is correct.
The notes state that higher categories are harder to define because they are aggregates of characters, so Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are factually correct, so options 2, 3 and 4 fail.
solution.common_trap: Mistaking Diptera for a family or Muscidae for an order.
solution.time_saving_tip: The suffix -idae marks a family in animals.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Binomial nomenclature
questions.question: The binomial system of nomenclature was given by

solution.key_concept: Binomial nomenclature was given by Carolus Linnaeus and is used worldwide.
steps: Recall that the binomial system was proposed by Linnaeus.
solution.why_not_others: The other scientists are known for other contributions, not for binomial nomenclature.
solution.common_trap: Associating any well-known biologist with nomenclature.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Binomial nomenclature
questions.question: Assuming it is printed in italics, which of the following scientific names follows the rules of binomial nomenclature?

solution.key_concept: The generic name comes first with a capital initial. The specific epithet comes second with a small initial.
steps: The genus Mangifera must start with a capital M.
The epithet indica must start with a small i and must follow the genus.
solution.why_not_others: Option 2 has a small initial for the genus. Option 3 has a capital initial for the epithet. Option 4 reverses the order of the two words.
solution.common_trap: Capitalising the specific epithet.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Binomial nomenclature
questions.question: In the scientific name Mangifera indica Linn., the word Linn. indicates
options: The family to which mango belongs
The abbreviated name of the author, Linnaeus
The place where the specimen was collected

solution.key_concept: The author's name is written after the specific epithet in abbreviated form.
steps: Linn. appears after the specific epithet indica.
It is the abbreviation for Linnaeus, the author.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): The abbreviated name of the author, Linnaeus
solution.why_not_others: The family of mango is Anacardiaceae. Neither a variety nor a collection place is cited in this position.
solution.common_trap: Reading the author citation as part of the classification.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Binomial nomenclature
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

solution.key_concept: The genus takes a capital initial and the epithet a small initial. ICBN governs plant names and ICZN governs animal names.
steps: Generic name begins with a capital letter (II).
Specific epithet begins with a small letter (IV).
ICBN gives the rules for naming plants (III).
ICZN gives the rules for naming animals (I).
solution.why_not_others: The other options swap the capitalisation rules, swap the two codes, or do both.
solution.common_trap: Confusing ICBN with ICZN.
solution.time_saving_tip: B stands for Botanical, so ICBN covers plants; Z stands for Zoological, so ICZN covers animals.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Binomial nomenclature
questions.question: Which of the following statements about binomial nomenclature are correct?

statements.A: Scientific names are in Latin or are Latinised, irrespective of their origin.
statements.B: When handwritten, the generic name and specific epithet are underlined together with a single continuous line.
statements.C: The first word of a scientific name represents the genus.
statements.D: Scientific names help avoid the confusion caused by local names.
statements.E: The author's name is written in full before the generic name.

options: A, C, D and E only

solution.key_concept: Binomial nomenclature follows universal rules on language, order of words, writing style and author citation.
steps: A is true: names are Latin or Latinised.
B is false: when handwritten, the two words are underlined separately.
C is true: the genus comes first.
D is true: scientific names avoid the confusion of local names.
E is false: the author's name is abbreviated and placed after the epithet.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A, C and D only
solution.why_not_others: Options 1 and 2 include B, which is false. Options 2 and 4 include E, which is false.
solution.common_trap: Underlining both words with a single line.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Five kingdom classification
questions.question: The five-kingdom classification, which included Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia, was proposed by:

solution.key_concept: R.H. Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom system in 1969.
steps: Linnaeus proposed only two kingdoms, Plantae and Animalia.
Whittaker proposed the five kingdoms in 1969.
solution.why_not_others: Linnaeus gave the two-kingdom system. Diener discovered viroids. Stanley crystallised viruses.
solution.common_trap: Crediting Linnaeus because he is the best-known name in classification.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Five kingdom classification
questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a kingdom of the five-kingdom system with the nature of its cell wall?
options: Monera – non-cellulosic cell wall (peptidoglycan in eubacteria)

solution.key_concept: Cell wall composition differs among the five kingdoms.
steps: Fungi have walls made of chitin.
Plants have walls made of cellulose.
Animals lack cell walls.
Monera have a non-cellulosic wall, which is peptidoglycan in eubacteria.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Monera – non-cellulosic cell wall (peptidoglycan in eubacteria)
solution.why_not_others: Options 1 and 2 swap chitin and cellulose. Animalia have no cell wall at all.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the wall materials of fungi and plants.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember the link: fungi go with chitin, plants with cellulose and animals with no wall.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Five kingdom classification
questions.question: Which set of entities is NOT placed in any kingdom of Whittaker's five-kingdom classification?

solution.key_concept: Viruses, viroids, prions and lichens are excluded from the five kingdoms.
steps: Bacteria, Mycoplasma and cyanobacteria belong to Monera.
Diatoms, slime moulds and protozoans belong to Protista.
Yeast, Penicillium and Agaricus belong to Fungi.
Viruses, viroids and lichens are not placed in any of the five kingdoms.
solution.why_not_others: Every other set belongs to Monera, Protista or Fungi.
solution.common_trap: Thinking that lichens go in Fungi or Plantae.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Five kingdom classification
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: In the five-kingdom classification, Chlamydomonas and Paramoecium are placed together in Kingdom Protista.
statements.R: Monera is the only kingdom of the five-kingdom system that contains prokaryotic organisms.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Protista groups unicellular eukaryotes, while Monera is the only prokaryotic kingdom.
steps: Protista brings together Chlamydomonas, Chlorella, Paramoecium and Amoeba, so A is true.
Monera is the only prokaryotic kingdom, so R is true.
A is explained by both organisms being unicellular eukaryotes, not by Monera being prokaryotic.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true, which rules out options 3 and 4. R does not explain why these two organisms are grouped together, which rules out option 1.
solution.common_trap: Choosing option 1 just because both statements are true and sound related.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Five kingdom classification
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: The two-kingdom system of Linnaeus successfully separated prokaryotes from eukaryotes but failed to separate unicellular from multicellular organisms.
statements.II: In the five-kingdom system, members of Kingdom Fungi show holozoic nutrition and have cell walls made of cellulose.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Shortcomings of the two-kingdom system and the defining features of fungi.
steps: The two-kingdom system failed to separate prokaryotes from eukaryotes. It also failed to separate unicellular from multicellular organisms. So I is incorrect.
Fungi are heterotrophic and absorptive, and their walls are made of chitin. Holozoic nutrition belongs to animals. So II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Each statement contains a false element, so no option that calls either statement correct can hold.
solution.common_trap: Accepting Statement I because its second half is true.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Monera, Protista and Fungi: salient features and classification
questions.question: Which organisms lack a cell wall, are the smallest living cells known and can survive without oxygen?

solution.key_concept: Mycoplasma are wall-less monerans.
steps: Mycoplasma lack a cell wall.
They are the smallest living cells and can survive without oxygen.
solution.why_not_others: Nostoc and Anabaena are cyanobacteria with a rigid wall. Methanogens are archaebacteria, which have a distinct cell wall.
solution.common_trap: Picking methanogens because they live without oxygen.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Monera, Protista and Fungi: salient features and classification
questions.question: Red tides in the sea are caused by:

solution.key_concept: Gonyaulax, a dinoflagellate, causes red tides.
steps: Dinoflagellates have two flagella and cellulose plates.
Rapid multiplication of Gonyaulax makes the sea appear red.
solution.why_not_others: Euglena does not cause red tides. Diatoms are chief producers in the oceans. Cyanobacteria form blooms, but these are not red tides.
solution.common_trap: Confusing cyanobacterial blooms with red tides.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Monera, Protista and Fungi: salient features and classification
questions.question: In which two classes of fungi does a dikaryotic (n+n) stage intervene between plasmogamy and karyogamy?

solution.key_concept: A dikaryophase occurs in Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes.
steps: Sexual reproduction in fungi follows the sequence plasmogamy, then karyogamy, then meiosis.
In Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes, an n+n dikaryotic stage occurs between plasmogamy and karyogamy.
solution.why_not_others: Deuteromycetes have only an asexual phase. Phycomycetes do not show this dikaryotic stage.
solution.common_trap: Including Deuteromycetes, which have no sexual stage at all.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Monera, Protista and Fungi: salient features and classification
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

solution.key_concept: Each class of fungi has typical example genera.
steps: Albugo belongs to Phycomycetes, so A-II.
Neurospora belongs to Ascomycetes, so B-IV.
Puccinia (rust) belongs to Basidiomycetes, so C-I.
Trichoderma belongs to Deuteromycetes, so D-III.
solution.why_not_others: Option 2 swaps the Ascomycete and Basidiomycete examples. Option 3 places Neurospora in Phycomycetes. Option 4 swaps Puccinia and Trichoderma.
solution.common_trap: Placing the rust fungus Puccinia in Deuteromycetes.
solution.time_saving_tip: Fixing Albugo as a phycomycete leaves only options 1, 2 and 4. Fixing Neurospora as an ascomycete then leaves options 1 and 4.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Monera, Protista and Fungi: salient features and classification
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Monera, Protista and Fungi are correct?

statements.A: Methanogens live in the gut of ruminants and produce methane in biogas.
statements.B: Euglenoids have a rigid cellulose cell wall.
statements.C: Chrysophytes have silica walls that form diatomaceous earth.
statements.D: Spores of slime moulds lack true walls and are easily destroyed.
statements.E: Basidiomycetes lack asexual spores and form basidiospores.

solution.key_concept: Salient features of monerans, protists and fungi.
steps: A is correct: methanogens live in the ruminant gut and produce methane.
B is wrong: euglenoids have a protein-rich pellicle, not a cell wall.
C is correct: chrysophyte silica walls form diatomaceous earth.
D is wrong: slime mould spores have true walls and are extremely resistant.
E is correct: Basidiomycetes lack asexual spores and form basidiospores.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options 2 and 3 contain the false statements B or D. Option 1 leaves out the true statement E.
solution.common_trap: Assuming euglenoids have a cell wall because they photosynthesise like plants.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Lichens
questions.question: The fungal component of a lichen is known as:

solution.key_concept: A lichen consists of a phycobiont (alga) and a mycobiont (fungus).
steps: The algal partner is the phycobiont.
The fungal partner is the mycobiont.
solution.why_not_others: The phycobiont is the alga. Mycorrhiza is a fungus and root association. Mycelium is a mass of hyphae.
solution.common_trap: Confusing mycobiont with mycorrhiza.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Lichens
questions.question: Lichens are good indicators of air pollution because they do not grow in areas with high levels of:

solution.key_concept: Lichens are absent where $SO_2$ pollution is high.
steps: Lichens are sensitive to pollution.
They are especially absent in areas with high $SO_2$.
solution.why_not_others: $CO_2$, $N_2$ and $O_2$ are normal components of air.
solution.common_trap: Picking $CO_2$ because it is often linked with pollution.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Lichens
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the roles of the partners in a lichen?
options: The fungus prepares food, while the alga absorbs water and minerals
The alga prepares food, while the fungus provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals
Both partners are autotrophic and share food equally
The alga provides shelter, while the fungus prepares food

solution.key_concept: Lichens show mutualism between an autotrophic alga and a fungus.
steps: The phycobiont (alga) is autotrophic and prepares food.
The mycobiont (fungus) provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): The alga prepares food, while the fungus provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals
solution.why_not_others: Fungi are heterotrophic, so they cannot prepare food. This rules out options 1, 3 and 4.
solution.common_trap: Reversing the roles of the two partners.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Lichens
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Lichens are very good indicators of air pollution.
statements.R: Lichens act as pioneers on bare rock during primary succession.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Lichens indicate pollution and also act as pioneer organisms.
steps: Lichens do not grow in polluted, $SO_2$-rich areas, so A is true.
Lichens are pioneers on bare rock, so R is true.
Being a pioneer does not explain sensitivity to pollution.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true, so options 3 and 4 are out. R gives no reason for pollution sensitivity, so option 1 is out.
solution.common_trap: Linking two true facts about lichens as cause and effect.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Lichens
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: In a lichen, the association between the alga and the fungus is so close that the lichen looks like a single organism.
statements.II: The association between a fungus and the roots of Pinus is a mycorrhiza and not a lichen.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Lichen versus mycorrhiza.
steps: The lichen association is so close that it appears as one organism, so I is correct.
Mycorrhiza is a fungus and higher plant root association, as in Pinus, so II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Both statements match the facts, so no option marking either as incorrect holds.
solution.common_trap: Calling the fungus and Pinus root association a lichen.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Viruses and viroids
questions.question: Viroids, the cause of potato spindle tuber disease, were discovered by:

solution.key_concept: T.O. Diener discovered viroids in 1971.
steps: Diener identified free infectious RNA as the cause of potato spindle tuber disease.
solution.why_not_others: Ivanowsky studied the tobacco mosaic agent. Stanley crystallised viruses. Beijerinck coined the term contagium vivum fluidum.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the scientists in the history of virology.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Viruses and viroids
questions.question: Bacteriophages usually contain which type of genetic material?

solution.key_concept: Plant viruses usually have ssRNA, while bacteriophages usually have dsDNA.
steps: A virus has either DNA or RNA, never both.
Bacteriophages usually carry double-stranded DNA.
solution.why_not_others: Single-stranded RNA is typical of plant viruses. The other two options do not describe bacteriophages.
solution.common_trap: Applying the plant virus pattern (ssRNA) to bacteriophages.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Viruses and viroids
questions.question: The causal agent of potato spindle tuber disease is:
options: An abnormally folded protein without nucleic acid
DNA enclosed in a protein capsid
A bacterium lacking a cell wall
Free RNA of low molecular weight lacking a protein coat

solution.key_concept: Viroids are free RNA molecules without a protein coat.
steps: Potato spindle tuber disease is caused by a viroid.
A viroid is free, low molecular weight RNA with no capsid.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Free RNA of low molecular weight lacking a protein coat
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 describes prions. Option 2 describes a virus. Option 3 describes Mycoplasma.
solution.common_trap: Confusing viroids with prions.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Viruses and viroids
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Showed that viruses could be crystallised

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Coined the term contagium vivum fluidum

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Found that the tobacco mosaic agent is smaller than bacteria

solution.key_concept: Key scientists in the history of virology.
steps: Ivanowsky (1892) found the tobacco mosaic agent is smaller than bacteria, so A-IV.
Beijerinck coined contagium vivum fluidum, so B-III.
Stanley crystallised viruses, so C-I.
Diener discovered viroids, so D-II.
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps Ivanowsky and Beijerinck. Option 2 swaps Beijerinck and Stanley. Option 3 swaps Stanley and Diener.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the contributions of Ivanowsky and Beijerinck.
solution.time_saving_tip: D-II (Diener and viroids) rules out option 3 straight away.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Viruses and viroids
questions.question: Which of the following statements about viruses, viroids and prions are correct?

statements.A: A virus contains both DNA and RNA enclosed in a capsid.
statements.B: Viruses are inert outside a host cell and are obligate parasites.
statements.C: Prions are abnormally folded proteins that cause BSE and Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease.
statements.D: Viroids have a protein coat and are larger than viruses.
statements.E: Mosaic formation, leaf rolling and vein clearing are symptoms of viral diseases in plants.

solution.key_concept: Distinguishing features of viruses, viroids and prions.
steps: A is wrong: a virus has either DNA or RNA, never both.
B is correct: viruses are inert outside a host and are obligate parasites.
C is correct: prions are misfolded proteins that cause BSE and CJD.
D is wrong: viroids lack a protein coat and are smaller than viruses.
E is correct: these are listed symptoms of viral disease in plants.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): B, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options 3 and 4 include the false statements A or D. Option 1 leaves out the true statement E.
solution.common_trap: Believing viroids have a capsid like viruses.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Plant kingdom: algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes and gymnosperms
questions.question: Agar, used in culture media and food preparations, is commercially obtained from which pair of algae?

solution.key_concept: Agar is obtained from the red algae Gelidium and Gracilaria.
steps: Agar is a red algal product.
Gelidium and Gracilaria belong to Rhodophyceae and are the sources of agar.
Laminaria, Fucus, Ectocarpus and Sargassum are brown algae. Spirogyra and Chara are green algae.
solution.why_not_others: Laminaria, Fucus, Ectocarpus and Sargassum are brown algae, which yield algin, not agar. Spirogyra and Chara are green algae and are not agar sources.
solution.common_trap: Confusing algin, which comes from brown algae, with agar, which comes from red algae.
solution.time_saving_tip: Agar and carrageen come from red algae. Algin comes from brown algae.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Plant kingdom: algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes and gymnosperms
questions.question: Which of the following algae shows a diplontic life cycle?

solution.key_concept: Life cycle patterns in algae: haplontic, diplontic and haplo-diplontic.
steps: A diplontic life cycle is seen in seed plants and in the brown alga Fucus.
Ectocarpus and Polysiphonia show a haplo-diplontic life cycle.
Spirogyra shows a haplontic life cycle.
solution.why_not_others: Ectocarpus and Polysiphonia are haplo-diplontic. Spirogyra is haplontic.
solution.common_trap: Assuming every brown alga has the same life cycle. Fucus is diplontic, but Ectocarpus and kelps are haplo-diplontic.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Plant kingdom: algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes and gymnosperms
questions.question: Which combination of photosynthetic pigments and stored food correctly characterises members of Rhodophyceae?
options: Chlorophyll a and c, fucoxanthin; laminarin
Chlorophyll a and d, r-phycoerythrin; floridean starch
Chlorophyll a and d, fucoxanthin; mannitol

solution.key_concept: Each algal class has a characteristic set of pigments and reserve food.
steps: Red algae (Rhodophyceae) have chlorophyll a and d along with r-phycoerythrin.
Their reserve food is floridean starch.
Chlorophyll a and c, fucoxanthin, laminarin and mannitol belong to brown algae. Chlorophyll a and b with starch belong to green algae.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Chlorophyll a and d, r-phycoerythrin; floridean starch
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 describes Phaeophyceae. Option 3 describes Chlorophyceae. Option 4 mixes red algal chlorophylls with the brown algal pigment fucoxanthin and the brown algal reserve mannitol.
solution.common_trap: Mixing pigments and reserve foods across the algal classes.
solution.time_saving_tip: Floridean starch is unique to red algae, so spotting it quickly gives the answer.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Plant kingdom: algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes and gymnosperms
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Selaginella and Salvinia are homosporous pteridophytes that produce only one kind of spore.
statements.R: Heterospory, seen in some pteridophytes, is considered a precursor to the seed habit.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Heterospory in Selaginella and Salvinia is a precursor to the seed habit.
steps: Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous, so they produce two kinds of spores. Assertion A is therefore false.
Heterospory in these plants is regarded as a precursor to the seed habit. Reason R is therefore true.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A is false but R is true
solution.why_not_others: A is false, so options 1, 2 and 3, which all require A to be true, are ruled out.
solution.common_trap: Assuming all pteridophytes are homosporous.
solution.time_saving_tip: Selaginella and Salvinia are the two standard examples of heterospory.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Plant kingdom: algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes and gymnosperms
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: In brown algae, the cellulosic cell wall is usually covered on the outside by a gelatinous coating of algin, and the zoospores are pear-shaped with two lateral flagella.
statements.II: Coralloid roots of Cycas are associated with cyanobacteria, whereas roots of Pinus are associated with mycorrhiza.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Wall structure and zoospores of Phaeophyceae; root associations in gymnosperms.
steps: Brown algae have a cellulosic wall, usually with an outer gelatinous coating of algin.
Their zoospores are pear-shaped and carry two laterally attached flagella. Statement I is correct.
Cycas has coralloid roots containing cyanobacteria, and Pinus has mycorrhizal roots. Statement II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Both statements match the facts, so any option that marks either statement as incorrect is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the associations, that is, linking cyanobacteria with Pinus and mycorrhiza with Cycas.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Animal kingdom: non-chordates up to phyla level
questions.question: Flame cells, which help in osmoregulation and excretion, are characteristic of which phylum?

solution.key_concept: Each non-chordate phylum has its own hallmark excretory structure.
steps: Flame cells are the excretory structures of flatworms (Platyhelminthes).
Annelids use nephridia, and arthropods use Malpighian tubules.
solution.why_not_others: Annelida have nephridia. Arthropoda have Malpighian tubules. Aschelminthes do not have flame cells.
solution.common_trap: Confusing flame cells with nephridia.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Animal kingdom: non-chordates up to phyla level
questions.question: A marine diploblastic animal with tissue level of organisation shows bioluminescence and has eight external rows of ciliated comb plates. It belongs to the phylum

solution.key_concept: Comb plates are the hallmark of Ctenophora (sea walnuts).
steps: Ctenophores are diploblastic and have tissue level of organisation.
They bear eight external rows of ciliated comb plates and show bioluminescence. Examples are Pleurobrachia and Ctenoplana.
solution.why_not_others: Cnidaria are also diploblastic with tissue level of organisation, but they have cnidoblasts, not comb plates. Porifera have only cellular level of organisation. Echinodermata are triploblastic.
solution.common_trap: Choosing Cnidaria because both phyla are diploblastic with tissue level of organisation.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Animal kingdom: non-chordates up to phyla level
questions.question: Which of the following non-chordates is monoecious?

solution.key_concept: Sexuality differs among annelids and aschelminths.
steps: Pheretima and Hirudinaria are monoecious annelids.
Nereis is a dioecious annelid.
Aschelminthes such as Ascaris and Ancylostoma are dioecious and show sexual dimorphism.
solution.why_not_others: Nereis, Ascaris and Ancylostoma all have separate sexes.
solution.common_trap: Assuming all annelids are monoecious and forgetting that Nereis is dioecious.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Animal kingdom: non-chordates up to phyla level
questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

solution.key_concept: Hallmark structures of non-chordate phyla and their representative animals.
steps: A radula is found in Mollusca, for example Pila: A-III.
A water vascular system is found in Echinodermata, for example Asterias: B-IV.
Choanocytes are found in Porifera, for example Spongilla: C-I.
Malpighian tubules are found in Arthropoda, for example Locusta: D-II.
solution.why_not_others: Option 2 swaps the molluscan and echinoderm examples. Option 3 swaps the sponge and insect examples. Option 4 gives the radula to an insect.
solution.common_trap: Linking the radula to echinoderms because both are marine invertebrates.
solution.time_saving_tip: Fix the easiest pair first. Choanocytes go only with sponges, which leaves options 1, 2 and 4.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Animal kingdom: non-chordates up to phyla level
questions.question: Which of the following statements about non-chordates are correct?

statements.A: True coelom and metamerism are both seen from phylum Annelida onwards.
statements.D: Obelia shows alternation between polyp and medusa forms, called metagenesis.
statements.E: Hemichordates possess a true notochord in the collar region.

solution.key_concept: Body cavity, excretion, metagenesis and the stomochord in non-chordates.
steps: A is correct. A true coelom is present from Annelida onwards, and metamerism is first seen in Annelida.
B is incorrect. Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomate, while Platyhelminthes are the acoelomates.
C is correct. Echinodermata have no excretory system.
D is correct. Obelia shows metagenesis.
E is incorrect. Hemichordates have a stomochord, not a true notochord.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A, C and D only
solution.why_not_others: Every other combination includes B or E, and both of these statements are false.
solution.common_trap: Treating the stomochord of Hemichordata as a notochord, or calling Aschelminthes acoelomate.
solution.time_saving_tip: Eliminate B and E first. Only one option contains neither of them.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Animal kingdom: chordates up to classes level
questions.question: Which of the following is a limbless amphibian?

solution.key_concept: Ichthyophis is the limbless member of class Amphibia.
steps: Ichthyophis is an amphibian and is limbless.
Hyla and Salamandra are amphibians with limbs.
Naja is limbless, but it is a reptile.
solution.why_not_others: Naja is a reptile, not an amphibian. Hyla and Salamandra are amphibians but have limbs.
solution.common_trap: Picking Naja simply because it is limbless, without checking its class.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Animal kingdom: chordates up to classes level
questions.question: A fish has a cartilaginous endoskeleton, placoid scales and a ventral mouth, and possesses an electric organ. It is most likely

solution.key_concept: Chondrichthyes features, and the special organs of Torpedo and Trygon.
steps: A cartilaginous skeleton, placoid scales and a ventral mouth place the fish in Chondrichthyes.
Among cartilaginous fishes, Torpedo has the electric organ.
solution.why_not_others: Trygon is cartilaginous but has a poison sting, not an electric organ. Exocoetus and Clarias are bony fishes (Osteichthyes).
solution.common_trap: Confusing Trygon's poison sting with Torpedo's electric organ.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Animal kingdom: chordates up to classes level
questions.question: In which of the following animals is the notochord present only in the larval tail?

solution.key_concept: Urochordata versus Cephalochordata.
steps: In urochordates such as Ascidia, the notochord is present only in the larval tail.
Cephalochordates such as Branchiostoma retain the notochord throughout life.
solution.why_not_others: Branchiostoma keeps the notochord throughout life. Petromyzon is a vertebrate, in which the notochord is replaced by a vertebral column. Balanoglossus has a stomochord, not a notochord.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up Urochordata and Cephalochordata.
solution.time_saving_tip: Uro means tail, so in urochordates the notochord is found in the tail only.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Animal kingdom: chordates up to classes level
questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.R: Reptiles have dry, cornified skin with epidermal scales or scutes.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Heart chambers and skin features of reptiles.
steps: Most reptiles have a three-chambered heart, but crocodiles have four chambers. A is true.
Reptilian skin is dry and cornified with epidermal scales or scutes. R is true.
The nature of the skin has nothing to do with the number of heart chambers, so R does not explain A.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 wrongly links skin structure to heart structure. Options 3 and 4 each mark a true statement as false.
solution.common_trap: Assuming all reptiles have a three-chambered heart.

questions.subject: biology
questions.topic: Animal kingdom: chordates up to classes level
questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Cyclostomes have a circular suctorial mouth without jaws, lack scales and paired fins, and migrate to fresh water for spawning.
statements.II: Members of class Chondrichthyes possess an air bladder and an operculum covering the gills.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Distinguishing features of Cyclostomata, Chondrichthyes and Osteichthyes.
steps: Cyclostomes (Petromyzon, Myxine) are jawless, with a circular suctorial mouth. They have no scales or paired fins and migrate to fresh water to spawn. Statement I is correct.
Chondrichthyes lack an air bladder. The operculum and air bladder are features of Osteichthyes. Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement II attributes bony fish features to cartilaginous fishes, so options 1 and 4 are wrong. Statement I is accurate, so option 2 is wrong.
solution.common_trap: Attributing the air bladder and operculum to all fishes.
